handbookNote: Iowa Code chapter 9B (Notarial Acts), Iowa's enactment of the Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts (2018) -- 32 operative sections (9B.1-9B.31 plus lettered inserts 9B.14A/B/C, 9B.21A/B; 4 sections reserved: 9B.3, 9B.19, 9B.22, 9B.29), fetched in full directly from legis.iowa.gov (https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/9B.pdf, Iowa Code 2026 compilation). CLASSIFICATION: application-only state -- confirmed directly from the full statutory text, not just prior scoping research. Section 9B.21(2) is the complete qualifications list for a base commission: age 18+, U.S. citizen/permanent resident, Iowa resident or Iowa place of employment/practice, able to read/write English, and not disqualified under 9B.23 -- plus an oath of office (9B.21(3)) and a $30 application fee (9B.21(1)). No exam and no pre-commission training course appear anywhere in chapter 9B for a standard commission. The ONLY 'training' language in the entire chapter is section 9B.14A(8)(a), which merely authorizes (does not require) the secretary of state to adopt rules that 'may' prescribe 'the means and process, including training requirements, of performing a notarial act involving a remotely located individual using communication technology' -- i.e. permissive rulemaking scoped narrowly to notaries who elect to perform remote online notarization (RON), not a base-commission requirement; a notary who never performs RON never encounters it. BOND: after reading the chapter's complete text (all 32 operative sections), chapter 9B contains NO surety bond requirement anywhere -- not in qualifications (9B.21), not in fees (9B.21B), not in discipline (9B.23). This affirmatively confirms, directly from the statute itself, the prior scoping finding that Iowa imposes no statutory bonding requirement for its base notary commission (a live sos.iowa.gov cross-check was still not obtainable due to persistent 403 responses; if the Secretary of State imposes a bond via administrative rule rather than statute, that would sit outside chapter 9B and would need a separate Iowa Administrative Code check). CONTENT DEPTH RATIONALE: Iowa is a comparatively short, clean, single-chapter statute with no exam layer and no training-course curriculum to test against -- unlike heavier-content states there is no secretary of state handbook or separate rules chapter with independently confirmed testable content. The bank is grounded entirely in chapter 9B's ~32 operative sections and totals 132 questions across 8 topic buckets (definitions; authority/requirements for notarial acts; notarial acts across jurisdictions; remote/electronic notarization -- the chapter's unusually detailed 12-subsection RON article, 9B.14A; certificates and official stamp; commissioning/qualifications/fees; discipline/database/prohibited acts; general provisions and validity) -- within this project's ~120-150 target range, not padded beyond what the statute supports, per the site owner's 'better nothing than nonsense' rule. PRICING: $0.75 (75 cents) -- re-tiered 2026-08-16 against the AL/FL/GA/TX reference range (those 4 education-only tracks landed at 138-224 questions after depth expansion); Iowa's real content ceiling (131 questions) sits below that range, so it takes the middle 'solid but lighter' tier rather than the top $0.99 tier (reserved for states whose real content lands within/close to 138-224, e.g. DE/NH/ND/VA/WA/WV) or the bottom $0.50 tier (reserved for genuinely thin states like MN). Still consistent with this project's practice of pricing application-only/no-assessment notary states below the $9.99 exam-state tier.
